nonblocking_findings: RA3-1 [Major] review-a: harness/model-guide-tests/guide.test.ts:676-756 (RA-2 case), comment at 728-731, and harness/model-guide/guide.ts:359. Evidence: the executed mutant N1 (guide.ts:359 row.tasks >= 5 changed to >= 4, real-work.ts unchanged) survives guide.test.ts with 17 passed (17). The cause: real-work.json lists t1/prod-tiny after the ranked rows (by_role.red order prod-evil rank 1, prod-one rank 2, prod-nine rank 3, prod-tiny rank null). guide.ts takes the first qualified row, so prod-one always comes before prod-tiny. Prod-one always qualifies, and prod-nine qualifies as the second choice. The comment 'a missing minimum picks t1/prod-tiny' is false for the guide.ts rule. The Red claim is true only with both minimums at 4 (mutant N3 fails 3 cases). The real-work.ts minimum alone (N2) already failed DS8, DS9, and DS10. The guide.ts rule can change a result: when at most one allowed red row has a rank, N1 gives prod-tiny as the pick or the second choice. Spec D18 pick rule: a model qualifies with 5 tasks or more in a producer row. Fix scope: Red adds a variant where t1/prod-nine is not allowed (or has no red row) and asserts second null. Red then confirms that N1 fails. Red corrects the comment.

RA3-2 [Nit] review-a: harness/model-guide-tests/guide.test.ts:651-655 and 699-706, and harness/model-guide/preview.sh:389. Evidence: the RA-1 case now puts a #variant route in the print-book audit pick, and mutants N4 (pick without audit_name) and N6 (audit_name without the # split) each fail 1 case. The second route kimi-code-plan-cn/k3.1-pro has no #variant, so mutant N5 (second cell with model_name, not audit_name) survives with 17 passed (17). Spec D17 and Q-S13 map each route key at render time. Fix scope: Red gives the second print-audit route a #variant suffix, for example kimi-code-plan-cn/k3.1-pro#high, and asserts Kimi K3.1 Pro.
